body:
I suggest we remove 13.4.7

_13.4.7 | Verify that all unneeded features, documentation, sample applications, configurations, and file or directory metadata (such as Thumbs.db, .DS_Store) are removed. | 3_

It's very low risk and doesn't usually pose a real security risk unless there is an exposureof versioning or config info, which is very rare.

comments.body: It is L3 - an extra step. Documentation, sample application etc may have information leakage and may provide some functionality that can be used against the application. It should stay as it is.

It's such a low risk item and ASVS is already close to 400 requirements that I am looking to whittle down some of these low risk requirements.

I do not think it should stay as is. I for sure think this is a solid candidate for removal.

Anyone else? @tghosth @danielcuthbert ?
Sample application inside some library folders, located in the public folder, etc. It is a real risk and I may even argue, it is worth L2.

> Documentation, sample application etc may have information leakage and may provide some functionality that can be used against the application

I have again never seen a breach of any kind due to missing documentation or exposed documentation.

And even if it were true, the documentation you worry about would be a vulnerability covered by another requirement. The documentation leak is not itself a vulnerability.
It should be watched as unintended information leakage requirement, but as it should be done in build step, it is located there.

> It should be watched as unintended information leakage requirement, but as it should be done in build step, it is located there.

All the more reason to remove it. We don't cover build processes in ASVS.

Nor does the requirement or anything else require anything to be done via the build process, but this is just a logical place to put a requirement in effect. We ask only that it be done, not where it should be done.

> Nor does the requirement or anything else require anything to be done via the build process, but this is just a logical place to put a requirement in effect. We ask only that it be done, not where it should be done.

This requirement still clearly says that (in part) we need a requirement about leaking documentation. I question the reasoning of that. Many frameworks do that on purpose. This does not apply to every app.

And again, these problems you worry about in this requirement are already covered by other requirements.

> And again, these problems you worry about in this requirement are already covered by other requirements.

Please map and list them.

Also, Thumbs.db and .DS_Store leaks are very low risk and don’t contain credentials or executable content.

At best they can reveal minor metadata like filenames or folder structures. This is not exploitable in a way that is not covered elsewhere.

This requirement really needs a major re-write or needs to go.

> > And again, these problems you worry about in this requirement are already covered by other requirements.
> 
> Please map and list them.

Documentation leaks are not themselves a vulnerability but would point to another vulnerability. So take your pick of any other technical requirement (other than the documentation ones).

> This requirement really needs a major re-write or needs to go.

Is this command?

> Please map and list them.

Sample applications?

> This requirement really needs a major re-write or needs to go.

How would you like to see this requirement being modified to be more focused (bear in mind we have a separate requirement about exposed source control folders)

> > This requirement really needs a major re-write or needs to go.
> 
> Is this command?

Yes, and it's an illustration of how you communicate to the ASVS team on a regular basis. It does not feel good. 

For example, here is a quote from you https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1438#issuecomment-2815863081

"I have tested and report it enough to say - this requirement stays and it is not a subject to be removed."

Is that a command? Looks like a command to me, Elar. What's good for the goose is good for the gander. If you are doing to dish it out you must also be willing to take it.

> > And again, these problems you worry about in this requirement are already covered by other requirements.
> 
> Please map and list them.

Here is an example. Suppose I leak Thumbs.db - that means I just leaked other files names in the directory. Suppose I can navigate to that file and access functionality I should not be able to access. Therefor it's actually an access control problem.

> > This requirement really needs a major re-write or needs to go.
> 
> How would you like to see this requirement being modified to be more focused (bear in mind we have a separate requirement about exposed source control folders)

I would accept:

_13.4.7 | Verify that any features, modules, or configuration settings not required for production are removed._

The documentation and Thumbs.db examples are poor and/or covered elsewhere.

> > > This requirement really needs a major re-write or needs to go.
> > 
> > 
> > How would you like to see this requirement being modified to be more focused (bear in mind we have a separate requirement about exposed source control folders)
> 
> I would accept:
> 
> _13.4.7 | Verify that any features, modules, or configuration settings not required for production are removed._
> 
> The documentation and Thumbs.db examples are poor and/or covered elsewhere.

Thanks for that. What do you think @elarlang?

> Verify that any features, modules, or configuration settings not required for production are removed.

The proposal says something different from what was targeted initially. The initial target is against enumeration and fingerprinting based on component documentation such as readme and license files, executing functionality from sample applications etc. For example, exposed Swagger UI documentation if it is not intended to be shared.

DS_Store and other examples do not matter too much, but _should_ be part of the cleanup.

~~Also, if to read the proposal, it requires quite a lot - removing all features, modules etc from any os, service, web server, framework, programming language that are not required, is not a realistic task.~~

> Also, if to read the proposal, it requires quite a lot - removing all features, modules etc from any os, service, web server, framework, programming language that are not required, is not a realistic task.

More so than the original requirement text?

Do you have a counter-proposal?

> Is that a command? Looks like a command to me, Elar. What's good for the goose is good for the gander. If you are doing to dish it out you must also be willing to take it.

That was precisely the reason I asked it :) (I skip at the moment the rest what I think about that)

---

> Do you have a counter-proposal?

> More so than the original requirement text?

Rechecking, it first felt more restrictive, maybe it is, but it is more how to interpret "all modules" part that triggers me for the first reaction. But I admit that "all unneeded features" basically means the same.

Current requirement: Verify that
* "all unneeded features" - this is vague and caused my to write: "removing all features, modules etc from any os, service, web server, framework, programming language that are not required, is not a realistic task."
* documentation - I interpret this as: readme, licence, changelog etc files, that reveal used verions AND Swagger UI as an example for "functional documentation"
* sample applications - sample snippets, demo scripts or whatever for components, problematic for php libraries.
* configurations - risk comes, when those are stored with accessible way
* and file or directory metadata (such as Thumbs.db, .DS_Store) are removed. - as I wrote, it is part of the hygiene to remove it, but can be taken as recommendation

---

> Here is an example. Suppose I leak Thumbs.db - that means I just leaked other files names in the directory. Suppose I can navigate to that file and access functionality I should not be able to access. Therefor it's actually an access control problem.

It is not part of the access control, as it is often static file served without application even involved. That was the reason why it was moved away from v4.0.3 access control section.

> > Is that a command? Looks like a command to me, Elar. What's good for the goose is good for the gander. If you are doing to dish it out you must also be willing to take it.
> 
> That was precisely the reason I asked it :)

I laughed hard when I read your response. And literally applauded you. Well done.

I know this is important to you so I am working to find a way to keep it in, @elarlang 

_Verify that no development‑ or documentation‑only artifacts are included in production. Examples include README, LICENSE, and CHANGELOG files; sample or demo code; Swagger UI; unused configuration files; and OS metadata such as.DS_Store, and Thumbs.db._

Is this is too much we can go back to your original requirement and I'll let this go so we can focus on more important things.

Related. https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1438#issuecomment-2823436919

> I'll re-analyze "the leftovers" from V13.4 and V13.5 and come up with a proposal on how to merge or reorganize them.

Proposal: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/3037

So the problem to solve here is to split potential code execution (that is worth L2) and potential information leakage, that is low-impact and most likely L3.

Requirement as it stands and items that will be covered (if agreed) by https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1438#issuecomment-2828236219 are ~~striked~~.

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **13.4.3** | Verify that all ~~unneeded features~~, documentation, ~~sample applications~~, configurations, and file or directory metadata (such as Thumbs.db, .DS_Store) are removed. | 3 | v5.0.be-14.1.6 |

It means, the most important part will be covered by other issue.

That leaves us:
* documentation - I interpret this as: readme, licence, changelog etc files, that reveal used verions AND Swagger UI as an example for "functional documentation"
* configurations - risk comes, when those are stored with accessible way, covered by current 13.5.5?
* and file or directory metadata (such as Thumbs.db, .DS_Store) are removed. - as I wrote, it is part of the hygiene to remove it, but can be taken as recommendation. covered by current 13.5.5?

We may say, that those leftovers are covered by other requirements:

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **13.5.4** | Verify that the application does not expose detailed version information of server-side components. | 3 | v5.0.be-14.3.3 |
| **13.5.5** | Verify that the web tier is configured to serve only files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional information, configuration, and source code leakage. | 3 | v5.0.be-14.3.5 |

The question is - if you read those requirements, do they covered the points above and is it actionable to build defenses based on that?

Tha main "leftover" from 13.4.3 is information leakage from documentation - changelog, readme, licence for components and version leakage (can be watched as covered by 13.5.4). But if Swagger UI or similar is exposed, is it documentation or part of https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1438#issuecomment-2828236219?

I think maybe the points in 13.4.3 could be merged into 13.5.5

For example:

"_Verify that the application is configured to only server files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional leakage of documentation (including private API definitions), directory metadata, configuration, and source code._"

Thinking more about it - I don't like to put any responsibility on 13.5.5, as this is "just in case requirement". The application should be safe also wihtout this requirement satisfied.

In case there are license, readme, or whatever files with .txt extension, then there is a high likelihood that .txt can not be disallowed, and it also does not cover this and does not solve the problem.

What throws me off is that I see documentation or Swagger published *on purpose* across millions of sites in the world of SaaS/PaaS.

What do we do when a requirement is not universally applicable?

> What do we do when a requirement is not universally applicable?

Say it in the requirement :) (https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1438#issuecomment-2823436919)

> > What do we do when a requirement is not universally applicable?
> 
> Say it in the requirement :) ([#1438 (comment)](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1438#issuecomment-2823436919))

Agreed

> Thinking more about it - I don't like to put any responsibility on 13.5.5, as this is "just in case requirement". The application should be safe also wihtout this requirement satisfied.
> 
> In case there are license, readme, or whatever files with .txt extension, then there is a high likelihood that .txt can not be disallowed, and it also does not cover this and does not solve the problem.

What do you propose instead?

To cover:
> documentation - readme, licence, changelog etc files, that reveal used verions AND Swagger UI as an example for "functional documentation"

Current requirement 13.5.4 addresses the technical information leakage related to the used components. All this readme, licence, and changelog for me is the same problem and same impact,t so I think those can be merged into this:
> 13.5.4 Verify that the application does not expose detailed version information of server-side components.

The question is, what to do with technical documentation - it is not about the used component versions, but the API or whatever other structure. Application must be secure when it is "open source" or the entire code-base is leaked, but in practice, it often helps to make attacks, and when this kind of documentation is available, it increases the likelihood of a successful attack.

Current situation:
> 13.4.7	Verify that all documentation, configurations, and file or directory metadata (such as Thumbs.db, .DS_Store) are removed.
@elarlang to prepare a proposal

> Verify that documentation (such as for internal API) and monitoring endpoints are not exposed unless explicitly intended.

So basically I address with this requirement things like Swagger and Spring Actuator, and it is L2 requirement.

title: 13.4.7 / v5.0.be-14.1.6 is low risk and can go
